summary.text: The candidates with the strongest convergent evidence as therapeutic targets are CA9 and CD70. Both are higher in tumour than in normal kidney at RNA and protein in CPTAC, the change replicates in TCGA-KIRC and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, single-cell data place CA9 in tumour cells, and both already have clinical-stage antibodies (girentuximab for CA9; cusatuzumab and vorsetuzumab for CD70). Neither is a selective DepMap dependency, so they are best read as surface handles for antibodies, conjugates, radioligands or imaging, not as genes the tumour needs to survive. CA9 carries a vital-organ caution (stomach) and is expressed in only about half of tumour cells; CD70 is shared with activated T cells.

A second tier comes from the target profile, whose leading positions are stable under random re-weighting: SCARB1, NNMT, SLC16A3 and ENPP3. NNMT is the most coherent of these: it is higher in tumour protein, its increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort, both single-cell datasets call it a tumour-cell gene, and higher expression goes with worse survival in TCGA, but it is an intracellular enzyme with no clinical drug. SCARB1 leads the target profile yet its cell attribution differs between the two single-cell datasets and it is enriched in adrenal gland; SLC16A3 is tumour-up and purity-robust but immune deconvolution assigns most of its transcripts to immune cells; ENPP3 already has an antibody-drug conjugate in trials but stains strongly in normal kidney. None of the four is a selective dependency.

The strongest biomarkers are genes lost in tumours, reflecting the loss of proximal-tubule identity rather than a druggable gain. PSAT1 is lower in tumours at protein and RNA, prognostic in TCGA, and its protein decrease replicates in the confirmatory cohort. PCK1 and ALDH6A1 are also lower in tumours and higher expression goes with better survival; ALDH6A1 sits on 14q, which is frequently lost. Among tumour-up genes, COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) ranks second overall and has the most developed mechanistic literature, but the survival claims in that literature are not reproduced by the TCGA Cox model. Literature and data also disagree for ABAT, where a paper claims poor prognosis with low expression in KIRC in a way that conflicts with the TCGA direction.

Because the convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, little-studied genes can only surface through the discovery screen, and two tumour-cell candidates are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1, a membrane collagen, is made mainly by RCC cells, its tumour increase replicates in TCGA and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, and its vital-organ RNA is low; what is missing is confirmed surface accessibility (SURFY and CSPA do not confirm it), protein staining in normal tissues, any selective dependency, confirmatory-cohort data and a measure of heterogeneity across tumour cells, and its AlphaFold model is low confidence. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also mainly RCC-derived, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, but it is probably intracellular, has no prognostic signal and no dependency. Immunohistochemistry on ccRCC and normal-tissue arrays, surface proteomics, and CRISPR knockdown in ccRCC lines or organoids would test them. Here novel means few ccRCC papers counted by gene symbol and no clinical drug; it does not mean nothing was published, and nothing here shows that targeting either gene would help a patient. The best stromal candidates (OLFML2A from fibroblasts, JAG2 from endothelium) are microenvironment hypotheses, and the immune-track leaders MILR1 and LILRB4 are driven by macrophage infiltration.

The established ccRCC biology frames these results. VHL is the recurrent driver and EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the approved drug target (belzutifan), with only a borderline DepMap dependency in two-dimensional culture; in single cells EPAS1 transcripts are mostly stromal and rarely detected in RCC cells, so its bulk RNA signal says little about the tumour-cell protein. Anti-angiogenic targets such as KDR are endothelial. In the treatment trials no gene separates the main arms after correction, so every treatment observation is an association, not a predictive biomarker.

omics.text: Seven up-regulated candidates are concordant across CPTAC RNA and protein and replicate in TCGA-KIRC: CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SLC16A3, SCARB1 and HK2. CA9 has the largest RNA change among them and NNMT the largest protein induction among the leading targets. ANGPTL4, a secreted HIF target, is up at both layers and is better read as a measurable biomarker of the VHL-HIF axis than as a target. HK2 and SLC16A3 fit the glycolytic, HIF-driven phenotype.

The leading biomarker-profile genes go the other way. PSAT1, PCK1 and ALDH6A1 are lower in tumours at protein, consistent with loss of normal proximal-tubule metabolism, and they are prognostic in TCGA-KIRC, with higher expression going with better survival for PCK1 and ALDH6A1. ALDH6A1 also shows frequent copy-number loss on 14q. Being down-regulated, these are biomarkers, not targets.

literature.text: Published support is strongest for CA9 (a CA9-targeted PET study showing proof-of-concept noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC) and CD70 (described as commonly overexpressed in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression, and the subject of CD70-specific single-domain antibody radiotracers). Both are early translational studies, not validated clinical biomarkers. For NNMT a paper reports tumour up-regulation and worse survival with high expression, which the TCGA data reproduce, and selective NNMT inhibitors exist as chemistry without ccRCC efficacy data.

Literature and data disagree in several places. The COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) literature is mechanistically rich (HIF-induced expression, a pro-glycolytic role and suppression of mitochondria-associated ferroptosis with LDHB) and claims poor survival, but the TCGA Cox association is not significant. For ABAT a pan-cancer paper claims poor prognosis in KIRC in a direction that conflicts with TCGA, and for MT1G a gene lower in tumour is linked to poor prognosis when high. SCARB1 and PIGR rank high on data with no literature relations in this corpus, and FABP1 papers concern colorectal cancer, so their positions rest on data rather than published ccRCC work.

external.text: Open Targets separates established from new targets. EPAS1 has an approved drug (belzutifan) and is the only leading gene with even a borderline ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency; VHL is the recurrent loss-of-function driver and the mechanistic rationale for HIF-2alpha inhibition, not a direct target. The surface antigens CA9 (girentuximab, Phase 3), CD70 (cusatuzumab, vorsetuzumab) and ENPP3 (AGS-16C3F) are tractable with antibodies but show no ccRCC dependency, so druggability rests on antigen access rather than on the tumour needing the gene.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) and SCARB1 are membrane proteins with predicted tractability but no clinical drug, and neither is a dependency; NNMT is cytoplasmic and has no drug returned. The normal-kidney loss genes ALDOB, SLC22A8 and COXFA4L2 carry drug annotations that are generic or non-oncology and do not imply ccRCC therapeutic rationale.

cells.text: CA9 and MET are tumour-intrinsic: RCC cells hold almost all CA9 tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and most MET transcripts [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935]. CA9 is detected in only about half of RCC cells, a heterogeneity that matters for antibody-based therapy. NNMT and CA9 are called tumour-cell genes in both single-cell datasets, whereas SCARB1 is myeloid-dominant in one dataset and RCC-dominant in the other, so its tumour-intrinsic status is unresolved.

Several bulk candidates are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is almost entirely endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951]. CD74 is a myeloid and B-cell gene and CXCR4 a lymphocyte gene, so their bulk signals reflect immune infiltration. EPAS1 transcripts are mostly stromal, with endothelial cells holding the largest share [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365]. HIF-2alpha is regulated post-translationally, so this does not argue against belzutifan. CD70 is expressed by RCC cells but also by Treg and other lymphocytes, and immune deconvolution assigns most CD70 and SLC16A3 bulk transcripts to immune cells, a conflict with their purity-robust tumour signal that needs direct single-cell checks.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, spots with high CA9 are enriched for RCC neighbours over random spots, and the composition-corrected expresser is the RCC cell rather than macrophages or endothelium, which agrees with the single-cell call. High-CD74 spots sit next to T cells, macrophages and dendritic cells, placing CD74 in immune niches. Spatial context was not run for MET, EPAS1 or KDR.

structure.text: Structural context is a descriptive monomer heuristic based on AlphaFold models and computationally detected cavities; it is not evidence of a degron, of ternary-complex formation or of degrader suitability, and no curated experimental degron reference was used for these candidates. The CA9 model is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]. Its top cavity has one nearby accessible lysine, and detected cavities recover about half of the experimental ligand-contact residues.

For the discovery candidates the structural information is weak. The COL23A1 model is low confidence and its only detected cavity is tiny and shallow, and a membrane collagen would be approached with antibodies, not small molecules. RAB42 is well modelled but its top cavity is small and shallow; a descriptive score does not imply druggability or degradability.

discovery.text: In the tumour-cell track, COL23A1 leads. It is a membrane collagen made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. Its tumour increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC and remains large when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It has few ccRCC papers, no clinical drug and low vital-organ RNA. What is missing is confirmed surface accessibility (UniProt annotates it as membrane, SURFY and CSPA do not confirm), any adverse survival signal, a selective DepMap dependency and a reliable structure [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91].

RAB42, the second tumour-track candidate, is a small GTPase made mainly by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. Its increase replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust, and it has very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is probably intracellular, its survival association is not significant and no dependency is shown, so it remains a hypothesis that would need functional knockdown before any drug discovery effort.

The stroma and immune tracks give microenvironment hypotheses rather than tumour-cell targets. OLFML2A is a secreted fibroblast gene and JAG2 an endothelial Notch ligand; both replicate in TCGA and are purity-robust, with no dependency evidence. The immune track, which holds most of the discovery pool, is led by the macrophage receptors MILR1 and LILRB4, and both are flagged as infiltration-driven: their bulk increase largely tracks macrophage content and largely vanishes when extrapolated to a pure tumour. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses, and none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: External replication and the purity check strengthen CA9, CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3 and SCARB1: their tumour increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, so it is not explained by infiltrating cells. Prognosis separates the candidates: higher NNMT goes with worse survival, while CA9, CD70 and COXFA4L2 have no significant TCGA Cox association, which weakens the survival claims made for CD70 and COXFA4L2 in the literature. The tubule-loss biomarkers PSAT1, PCK1 and ALDH6A1 are prognostic. Among the discovery leaders, MILR1 and LILRB4 are weakened by the purity check because their increase is infiltration-driven.

VHL is the only confirmed recurrent somatic driver among the leading genes, and no leading candidate is a selective DepMap dependency; EPAS1 is borderline. Protein-adjusted kinase activity was not queried in this run. In the confirmatory DIA cohort the protein changes of SCARB1, NNMT and PSAT1 replicate in direction and significance. CA9 was not measurable there, which is not a failure to replicate, and HK2, ENPP3, CD70 and SLC16A3 were not profiled in that cohort in this run, so their protein calls rest on the discovery cohort only.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, the target profile is stable at the top: SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay in the target top ten in most draws with narrow rank intervals. In the biomarker profile only PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are similarly robust, while ALDH6A1, PPP1R1A and NNMT have wide intervals. In the overall convergence ranking CA9 and COXFA4L2 are the robust leaders.

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. PIGR has the widest interval among the overall top ten and, like SCARB1, would leave the overall top 25 without the genetics stream. NNMT and UMOD depend on literature, FABP1 and NPHS2 on omics, and SLC16A3 and HK2 would drop out of the target top 25 without the tumour-up omics stream. These candidates should be read as weight-sensitive.

treatment.text: In the treatment-response cohorts every observation is an association, and no gene separates the main arms after correction. In IMmotion150, CA9 is associated with longer benefit on the combination, atezolizumab and sunitinib arms, but the combination-versus-sunitinib difference is not significant [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. NNMT is associated with earlier progression in the CheckMate-025 nivolumab and everolimus arms, again with no significant arm difference [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]. PSAT1 shows the same pattern [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]. None of these is a treatment-selection biomarker, and the Choueiri nivolumab cohort is small.

subtypes.text: PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant than in wild-type tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711]. It is not flagged as a subgroup target because the CPTAC protein difference is not significant. EPAS1 is lower in ccB than ccA tumours and helps define the ccA/ccB split [gene=EPAS1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-0.935]. NNMT shows no significant VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 difference, so its increase looks pan-subtype. Subtype differences in bulk tissue can partly reflect different immune and stromal content, and PCK1, SLC16A3 and several ranked biomarkers were not profiled by subtype.

adc.text: For antibody-drug conjugates or radioligands, CD70 has a surface call, no vital-organ proteome enrichment and one of the top suitability scores, but no Human Protein Atlas staining data, so normal-tissue safety is only partly assessed. CA9, a known target used here as a control, has a surface call but high staining in stomach and is expressed by only a minority of tumour cells in the weakest quarter of donors, which limits homogeneous targeting. ENPP3, the target of AGS-16C3F, is observed at the surface but stains at the maximum level in normal kidney and duodenum. SCARB1 is observed at the surface but is enriched in adrenal gland, an on-target, off-tumour concern. A high suitability score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Immune deconvolution assigns most CD70 bulk transcripts to immune cells, and CD70 correlates positively with CD8 and regulatory T cells, so it is as much an immune-axis gene of T-cell-infiltrated tumours as a tumour-cell antigen. FCGR3A tracks the immune score closely and works as an infiltration control: its tumour increase reflects immune content, not tumour-cell expression. SLC16A3 is also assigned mostly to immune cells despite a near-zero CD8 correlation and a purity-robust tumour signal, a conflict that remains unresolved. In single cells, CD74 (myeloid and B cells) and CXCR4 (lymphocytes) are immune-compartment genes whose bulk levels rise with infiltration.

integration.text: The layers converge most clearly on CA9: omics, replication, purity, single-cell and spatial data, literature and clinical-stage drugs all point the same way, and the only gaps are dependency, heterogeneity and stomach expression. CD70 converges on omics, replication, literature and drugs but is shared with T cells. NNMT converges on omics, prognosis, confirmatory replication and single-cell tumour attribution, and is the strongest candidate that is both a prognostic biomarker and a possible small-molecule target. SCARB1 converges on data streams and genetics but lacks literature and a consistent cell attribution.

The candidates fall into three groups. Targets are tumour-up surface or tractable proteins (CA9, CD70, ENPP3, SCARB1, SLC16A3) plus the established EPAS1 axis. Biomarkers are mostly tubule-loss genes (PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB, SLC22A8), which are measurable and prognostic but not druggable gains, together with COXFA4L2 and ANGPTL4 as tumour-up markers. VHL is mechanism, and KDR, CD74 and CXCR4 are microenvironment genes. The main disagreements are between literature survival claims and TCGA (COXFA4L2, CD70, ABAT) and between bulk purity and immune deconvolution for SLC16A3 and CD70.

targets.rationale: Strongest overall convergence: tumour-up at RNA and protein, replicated in TCGA, purity-robust, tumour-cell expressed in both single-cell datasets and in situ, with clinical-stage antibodies and imaging literature. Not a dependency, expressed in about half of tumour cells and enriched in stomach, so best used as an antibody, radioligand or imaging handle.

Tumour-up at RNA and protein, replicated and purity-robust, surface protein without vital-organ proteome enrichment and with clinical-stage antibodies. Shared with activated T cells and lacking normal-tissue staining data; no dependency.

Placed above SCARB1 despite a lower target-profile rank because more independent layers agree: protein induction confirmed in the DIA cohort, tumour-cell attribution in both single-cell datasets, adverse prognosis in TCGA and concordant literature. Intracellular enzyme with no clinical drug and no dependency.

Top of the target profile and robust to re-weighting; surface HDL receptor whose protein increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort. Ranked below NNMT because its cell attribution differs between single-cell datasets, it is enriched in adrenal gland, it has no ccRCC literature and its overall rank depends on the genetics stream.

Established target with an approved drug (belzutifan) downstream of VHL loss and the only leading gene with a borderline selective DepMap dependency; included as the clinical reference. Its bulk RNA is mostly stromal in single cells, so its convergence score understates it.
Tumour-up, replicated surface ectoenzyme with an antibody-drug conjugate (AGS-16C3F) already tested. Maximum staining in normal kidney and duodenum and no dependency argue for caution.

MCT4 lactate exporter, tumour-up at RNA and protein, replicated and robust in the target profile, membrane-located with predicted tractability. Immune deconvolution assigns most of its transcripts to immune cells, a conflict with its purity-robust signal, and it has no clinical drug or dependency.
Most robust biomarker-profile gene: lower in tumours at protein and RNA, prognostic in TCGA, with the protein decrease replicated in the confirmatory cohort. No treatment-selection value.
Robust tubule-loss biomarker, lower in tumours at protein and RNA, with better survival for higher expression in TCGA. Not profiled in the confirmatory or subtype layers.
Lower in tumours at protein, on frequently lost 14q, with better survival for higher expression; a loss-of-identity prognostic marker whose biomarker rank is weight-sensitive.

Second in the overall ranking and robust there, tumour-up and purity-robust with rich mechanistic literature. Kept as a biomarker because published survival claims are not reproduced in TCGA and there is no dependency or specific drug.

Exploratory: leading tumour-track discovery candidate, made mainly by RCC cells, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust with low vital-organ RNA; main limitation is unconfirmed surface accessibility and no dependency or functional evidence.

Exploratory: second tumour-track discovery candidate, RCC-derived, replicated and purity-robust with almost no ccRCC literature; main limitation is a probably intracellular small GTPase with no prognostic signal or dependency.

limitations.text: Bulk tumour-versus-normal comparisons mix tumour-intrinsic change with loss of normal tubule cells and gain of immune and stromal cells; purity extrapolation and single-cell data reduce but do not remove this.

No leading candidate except EPAS1 (borderline) is a selective DepMap dependency, and two-dimensional cell lines miss HIF-2 biology, so therapeutic claims rest on antigen access, prognosis and drug history rather than functional requirement.

Several layers were not run for every candidate within the call budget: kinase activity, STRING, confirmatory-cohort data for CD70, ENPP3, SLC16A3 and HK2, spatial context for MET, EPAS1 and KDR, and normal-tissue staining for CD70.
Treatment-response findings are associations; no gene separates the main arms after correction and one cohort is small.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; literature novelty is counted by gene symbol and earlier preclinical work was not systematically checked.
Structural scores are descriptive monomer heuristics and are not evidence of a degron or degrader suitability.

Several agent statements had bare numbers next to their bound annotations and were reworded to remove the duplicates before verification; the bound values were kept. Passing the automatic checks is not complete scientific validation.
